text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty SEV2 -> #incidents. Multiple customer 5xx spikes from edge POP eu-west1 detected (http 502/504). Alert group: EDGE-HTTP-5XX. Root alert at 1853007777.

Jordan (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing a spike in 502s from eu-west1 in the dashboard. Rolling up to incident.

Anna (support): Customers are reporting timeouts in EU web apps, a handful on official support queue. Example: customer-chi reported huge 502 burst at 09:12 UTC.

Maya (sre): Can we confirm whether it's origin failures or edge-level? I see backend health checks green, but edge return codes increasing.

Rob (runtime): Quick check: generation traffic to eu-west1 shows increase in token latency and 504s. No recent deploys from runtime in the last 3 hours.

Eli (netops): I'm pulling netflow. Initial glance shows packet loss between our POP and upstream ISP AS12345 starting ~09:10 UTC. Possible partial fiber flap or BGP dampening.

Jordan (oncall): @Eli can you paste traceroute/mtr to one of impacted POP egress IPs?

Eli (netops): mtr to 34.89.12.7 (edge-eu-west1-egress):

-----BEGIN MTR-----
HOST: 34.89.12.7  Loss%  Snt  Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1.|-- 10.0.0.1   0.0%   10   0.5   0.6   0.4   1.2   0.3
 2.|-- 52.23.45.1  0.0%   10   1.2   1.4   1.1   2.0   0.3
 3.|-- 198.51.100.9 24.0%   10  50.4  52.0  48.9  200.1  40.0
 4.|-- 34.89.12.7  0.0%   10  12.3  15.1  12.1  70.2  18.5
-----END MTR-----

Eli (netops): Note hop 3 is an upstream AS that is showing packet loss/lossy latencies.

Maya (sre): That matches edge return codes. Likely last-mile/upstream. We should engage ISP and start traffic reroute plan.

Jordan (oncall): Assigning tasks: Eli -> confirm upstream AS issue & open ticket with ISP; Maya -> implement temporary traffic steering to avoid affected upstream; Rob -> adjust edge caching TTLs and enable extra retries to reduce user-visible errors; Anna -> keep customers updated.

Eli (netops): Opening ticket with provider: INC-9921 to AS12345. Provider initial reply: "We observe partial packet loss on peering to AWS eu-west1 region, investigating." They asked for timestamps and sample flows which I've sent.

Maya (sre): I'm going to flip routing preference in our SmartRouting policy for eu-west1 to prefer peering via AS67890 (secondary transit) for HTTP egress. Rolling change via control-plane:```
# routing-policy update
smart_routing.zone.europe.preferred_path = ["AS67890","AS12345"]
# quick apply
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/routing/apply -d '{"zone":"europe","policy":"prefer_secondary"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $INC_TOKEN"
```

deploy-bot: Routing change started (change-id: rc-2026-03-15-001).

Maya (sre): Applying canary first to 10% of eu-west1 traffic. Monitoring.

Jordan (oncall): Anna, any worsening reports?

Anna (support): New ticket from enterprise-corp: repeated 502s, but says intermittent — same time window. I'm sending their session IDs to SRE for request traces.

Rob (runtime): Increasing edge retry count for generation endpoints from 2 -> 4 and enabling short backoff. Pushing config to eu-west1 only:```
edge.retry.count=4
edge.retry.backoff=150ms
```

Maya (sre): Canary shows error rate drop from 8% -> 2.3% in the 10% cohort after reroute. Continuing to 50% if no regression.

Eli (netops): ISP says they implemented temporary micropatch on peering node; still seeing intermittent packet loss but at reduced rate. They've requested we keep traffic on alternate path where possible.

Jordan (oncall): Can we failover fully to AS67890 for the eu-west1 egress for the next 30 minutes? If stable, we'll keep longer and coordinate provider maintenance window.

Maya (sre): Rolling to 100% now. deploy-bot: Routing change rc-2026-03-15-001 -> completed for zone europe (eu-west1: 100%).

Rob (runtime): After full failover, observed client-side 5xx down to baseline ~0.5% within 5 minutes. Token latency median improved ~40ms.

Anna (support): Informing impacted customers: draft message posted to support channel for review.

Jordan (oncall): Good. Next: 1) Keep monitoring for 30m 2) Ask ISP for root-cause and ETA for restoration 3) Prepare rollback plan if secondary path degrades.

Eli (netops): ISP update: root cause likely flapping micro-BGP session on one of their nodes after maintenance. They've scheduled mediator patch in 2 hours. They will keep us posted.

Maya (sre): I'm creating an alert to detect if path via AS67890 deteriorates (increase in RTT or packet loss). If it breaches thresholds, auto-roll back to AS12345 and throttle traffic to prevent cascading failures.

Jordan (oncall): On-call handoff: I'll stay for the next 45 minutes then hand to Maya. @Maya you'll take follow-up once my shift goes.

Maya (sre): Acknowledged, taking post-incident ownership. I'll compile timeline and blameless RCA after ISP confirms root cause.

Anna (support): Customer comms sent. Affected tenants got a note with expected follow-up once provider updates.

incident-bot: Incident SEV2 -> mitigated. Mitigation action: traffic reroute to AS67890. Time to mitigation ~10m. Marking timeline entry.

Jordan (oncall): Closing active pager. Leaving a follow-up checklist: postmortem, provider RCA, change to routing policy to add tolerance for single-as failure, and revisit SLA impact.

Maya (sre): I'll schedule a postmortem doc and include packet captures, mtr, and our reroute timeline.

Eli (netops): Saved mtr/traces to /mnt/logs/incidents/1853007777/ and shared with ISP.

Rob (runtime): No code changes required. Will keep edge retry change for 1 hour and then revert if not needed.

Anna (support): Closing customer tickets as mitigated where appropriate; keeping one enterprise case open until final RCA.

Jordan (oncall): Thanks everyone. Handing off to Maya for RCA and long tail monitoring. :white_check_mark:
